title: Add transitive dependency prober and sprinkle CI hygiene
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight transitive dependency prober (opt-in) for presubmit and consolidates a few CI hygiene checks. No breaking user-facing changes.
description: Motivation: CI flakes and slow presubmit cycles have been traced to subtle transitive dependency churn and a couple of poorly-scoped release hooks. This PR introduces a compact 'dep-prober' tool that statically inspects lockfiles (yarn.lock, poetry.lock, go.sum) and reports likely transitive upgrade vectors and duplication hotspots. It also standardizes two small CI hygiene points: a lightweight release-check scaffold that enforces release-note metadata on release branches, and minor cleanup of legacy release hooks that caused duplicate artifact uploads. Scope: - dep-prober (Go) + lightweight runner: scans lockfiles, produces a JSON summary (used by presubmit) and a terse human-friendly summary in CI logs - presubmit integration: warn-by-default step (does not block on first rollouts) and an opt-in strict gating mode for release teams - release-check scaffold: small GH Action that validates release metadata and consistent artifact names - removed legacy 'release-hook.sh' adapter and migrated callers to the new scaffold - unify lint runners under a single composite action to reduce startup overhead and make cache keys predictable (no behavior changes) Checklist: - [x] dep-prober implementation and unit tests - [x] presubmit integration and pipeline test - [x] migration of release hooks and docs update - [x] reviewer signoffs - [x] CI green after rerun Compatibility: dep-prober defaults to soft-failure to avoid breaking existing workflows; teams can opt into strict mode via repository-level config. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable soft warnings for 2 weeks, then invite teams to flip strict gating via a Linear-backed opt-in process. Related: ENG-1122 for broader dep curation work; SUP-934 incident triage for release-hook flakiness.
